note: The app-loop checks that still fail under schwunggrid=page. Started at 13 (Phase 0); SP-11 took it to 6, SP-17 to 5, the SP-17 fix round to 3. All three left are ONE thing, and it is a FIXTURE limit rather than a movy defect: under `page` the page SET is Schwung's, planned from the module's own declared hierarchy, and the module these three use — the suite's `mrdrums` fixture (the one `browser-test/mock-synth.mjs` declares) — declares NO `ui_hierarchy` at all, so the plan is the single fallback page 'Main' while movy's own config gives it four banks (Main/Rand/Global/Preset). READ BACK, not remembered: `app-loop.mjs` prints a permanent `[page-plan]` line on both arms, and with this fixture and no pin it says `mode=page lib=true movyBanks=4 claimed=true delegated=true ctlPages=1 names=["Main"]`. The preset-browse block turns the jog three times to reach a Preset page Schwung never plans, and 'held-step jog switches page' steps off page 0. THE CONSEQUENCE, stated so it is not read as a general absolution: under `page` the only source of a page is the module's own declaration, so a bank or cell that exists ONLY in movy's config (`src/modules/*.json`) is on no page at all. What that costs is owned by SP-32 in docs/schwung-page-migration.md — it is NOT the same statement as 'not a movy defect', and the fixture above is the narrow instance of it, not the whole. Said of THAT fixture and not of the suites' modules at large — a fixture that DOES declare a hierarchy, like `hier_params_overflow_two_levels`, plans two pages under `page` and is not what these labels run on. THIS LIST MAY SHRINK AND MUST NEVER GROW. A label here that starts passing must be DELETED (the run fails until it is). A failure not listed here is a regression and fails the run. Two labels left at the fix round — 'Back leaves the file browser' and 'select committed the preset path' — and they left because the block that asserts them is now GATED on its own premise (`appState.currentView === VIEW_FILE_BROWSE`), not because what they assert started holding under `page`: they were passing vacuously, on a browser that never opened.
